items.entity: prescribed material volume V (sum of rho_i = V)
items.description: Problem (1) uses sum(rho_i)=V and the initial guess rho_i=V/m (Secs. 3.2, 4.1), but no numerical value of V or V/m is given for CANT-16-2-2-5 in Sec. 7, Sec. 7.1 or Table 1. Because stiffness is linear in rho, only the ratio V/(m*rho_bar) affects the layout.

Problem (1), the dual (2) and the DOC clipping in Algorithm 4 all use an upper bound rho_bar_i, but its value is never stated (Sec. 7.1 gives only the lower bound). With V fixed, rho_bar sets the effective volume fraction V/(m*rho_bar) and decides how many elements reach full material.
readings: rho_bar large enough to be practically inactive

items.description: Sec. 7.1 gives three values for this one example: 0 for PBM, 1e-7 for IP and DOC, and 1e-3 for an extra IP run whose objective (66.1989) the paper itself calls not comparable. A single-solver rerun has to pick one, and a displacement-based solver cannot use 0 because K would be singular.

items.entity: z-direction load 'in the middle of the right-hand face'
items.description: Sec. 7 says only that 'a load in direction z is applied in the middle of the right-hand face (Figure 2(a))' and refers to Fig. 2 for the specifications. Whether this is a single nodal force, a line load or a small patch, and its exact footprint, is shown only in the figure. The bridge load, by contrast, is explicitly a uniform load on a rectangle.
readings: single nodal force at the face-centre node (y = 0.5W, z = 0.5H)
line load along y through the face centre (at z = 0.5H)
line load along z through the face centre (at y = 0.5W)
uniform load on a small square patch centred on the face (e.g. 2x2 or 4x4 fine elements)

items.entity: z-direction load on the right-hand face
items.description: No load magnitude is given in Sec. 7, Sec. 7.1 or Table 1. The reported objective 1/2 f^T u = 66.19... scales with its square.
readings: total force 1 split equally over the loaded nodes

items.entity: Young's modulus E of the solid behind K_i
items.description: The constitutive data behind the element matrices K_i are never given (Secs. 1, 6.2, 7). Compliance scales as 1/E.
Not stated anywhere. Unlike E, it changes the 3D element stiffness K_i non-proportionally, so it can shift the optimal density distribution.

items.entity: physical size of the 16x2x2 cuboid / element edge length
items.description: Sec. 7 defines the domain as m_x x m_y x m_z cubes 'of equal size', which fixes the aspect ratio at 8:1:1 and the mesh at 256x32x32, but never gives the cube edge length. For 3D trilinear hexahedra the element stiffness scales with edge length h, so compliance scales as 1/h.
readings: coarse cube edge = 1 (domain 16x2x2, fine element edge 1/16)

items.entity: convergence/stopping tolerance that defines the reference design
items.description: Table 1 reports seven runs for this example (PBM duality gap 1e-5 and 1e-6, IP 1e-5, DOC ||rho+ - rho||_inf of 1e-2, 1e-3 and 1e-5), with objectives from 66.1927 to 66.2107. Sec. 7.1 and Fig. 3 (shown for CANT-16-2-2-4, not -5) say loose DOC tolerances give visibly different designs; only DOC 1e-5, PBM and IP are called 'visually identical'. The tolerance a rerun should use is not fixed.

No filter is mentioned anywhere. Formulation (1) (linear VTS, K(rho) = sum rho_i K_i, i.e. p = 1) and the DOC update in Algorithm 4, adapted from top88, contain none, so 'no filter' is the implied reading. Standard SIMP-type codes apply one by default, though, and the text never says explicitly that it is off.
readings: sensitivity filter, radius about 1.5 fine elements
density filter, radius about 1.5 fine elements
